mutations.name: D1 original defect: store honoured only when STRICTLY false — "false"/0/"no"/null all get retained
D1 over-reach in the other direction: absent store reads as opted out, so every default client stops chaining
D1 truthiness instead of a token list: "false" is a non-empty string, so the string spelling is retained again
D1 no case folding — "FALSE" stops being an opt-out
D1 numeric 0 stops opting out
D2 original defect: the field walk only looks at the top level, so array content is invisible again

SURVIVOR (documented): D2 picks the FIRST oversized field instead of the largest. This is an efficiency term, not a correctness one: trimContentToFit now runs until CONVERGENCE and every pass strictly shortens the chosen field, so the entry reaches the cap regardless of which candidate is picked first. Measured with the mutation applied — five 60000-char array fields (worst case for first-candidate) still settle under a 102400 MAX_ENTRY_BYTES; picking the largest converges in fewer passes, which no assertion observes. If the loop ever regains a fixed pass bound, re-run this mutation.
D2 tool_call_id becomes shrinkable — cutting it orphans the tool result from its call
D2 the block discriminator becomes shrinkable — a truncated `type` is no longer a text/image_url block
D2 the copy-on-write write becomes an in-place one — the caller's own request messages get rewritten

D4 original defect: the lookup path stops checking the absolute bound, so read-refresh makes retention unbounded again
D4 the absolute bound is measured from lastAccess, so a read refreshes it and it collapses into the idle timeout
D4 a same-id refresh restarts the absolute clock — re-writing an id resets its age
D4 the default bound shrinks to a minute — a long agent session would be dropped mid-run
D4 the env override is ignored — the knob exists but does nothing
D3+D4 the sweep stops checking the idle timeout — an abandoned entry sits until the absolute bound
D4 the sweep stops checking the absolute bound — an entry nobody reads is never age-collected
stats stop reporting the absolute bound — an operator asking how long a conversation is kept only sees the idle half
